title: How do Transformers Perform Low-Level Control In-Context?
abstract: arXiv:2611.07291v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: One of the remarkable abilities of Transformer-based neural networks is in-context learning. This motivates us to think about "in-context" control. Can we control a system knowing only (1) that it belongs to a particular family of systems and (2) some data on system evolution (provided as the context trajectory) but no specific parameter information? Specifically, we investigate the ability of Transformer-models to perform "in-context" control of unstable, nonlinear dynamical systems, where context consists only of the unforced system dynamics. We leverage a multi-head, GPT-2-style architecture, and we evaluate performance for two classical nonlinear systems -- the cartpole system and the two-link acrobot system, where the system parameters are unknown to the Transformer. tldr: 该论文研究了GPT-2风格的Transformer如何仅凭无外力的系统演化轨迹作为上下文，在不掌握具体参数的情况下实现对未知参数的不稳定非线性系统（小车倒立摆与Acrobot）的上下文学习式控制。
en_tdlr: This paper investigates how a GPT-2-style Transformer can perform in-context control of unstable nonlinear systems (cartpole and acrobot) with unknown parameters, using only unforced system dynamics trajectories as context and expert controller data available solely at training time.
